principles: Honest-unavailable: a failure event only ever refines the REASON of an unavailable final; usage numbers are never fabricated and a genuine turn.completed usage always records provider-reported unchanged
Bounded memory: every retained byte obeys the existing 1MiB last-one-wins UsageLineScanner cap discipline; no transcript or session-file persistence
Diagnosability over compactness: the digest is a short sanitized human-readable excerpt of error.message (innermost message when nested JSON), not a hash
Fail honest on degradation: when the failure line is over-cap dropped or carries no extractable message, degrade to an explicit generic token instead of guessing
drivers: The usage lane's F-013/F-026 truncation semantics and provider-reported path must stay byte-identical
A single retained line is the parse target for fake (full-buffer) and streaming (retained-line) runners alike, so the failure scan must accept both shapes
codex-only scope with no ledger schema change (unavailableReason is already a free non-empty string)

options.name: second-bounded-lane
pros: Reuses UsageLineScanner unchanged (two instances), preserving cap + last-wins discipline per lane
Usage candidate can never be evicted by a later failure line, so provider-reported behavior is untouched
Failure line surfaces as a separate HostRunSpawnResult.failureText field; fake runners stay valid without changes (core falls back to scanning their full stdout)
cons: Adds a second scanner instance (up to ~2MiB extra bounded state) and one new result field

options.name: widen-single-retainer
pros: No new plan/result fields; one scanner instance
cons: last-one-wins across mixed event types lets a trailing turn.failed evict a genuine turn.completed usage candidate, silently converting a provider-reported final into unavailable (dishonest usage loss)
Entangles the F-013/F-026 truncation flag with failure lines, changing existing semantics

options.name: persist-full-transcript
pros: Complete forensics for any future failure shape
cons: Breaks the bounded-memory design (flooding host exhausts memory or disk)
Violates the --ephemeral no-session-file expectation and stores prompt/output content the ledger deliberately avoids

rationale: Only the second bounded lane keeps both invariants at once: the usage lane (and its truncation semantics) stays byte-identical so provider-reported finals can never regress, while the failure lane gets the identical 1MiB last-one-wins discipline for bounded honest reason enrichment. Unknowns resolved with it: (1) digest = innermost error.message when the message parses as nested JSON, control chars/whitespace collapsed, truncated to 160 chars with a trailing ellipsis marker; (2) a failure event with no extractable message records turn_failed(no_error_message); (3) an over-cap-dropped failure line honestly falls back to no_turn_completed_usage_event (no new truncation marker — the reason enrichment is best-effort diagnostics, never load-bearing state).

preMortem.scenario: A trailing turn.failed after a genuine turn.completed downgrades a provider-reported final to unavailable
preMortem.trigger: Multi-turn codex stream where an earlier turn completed with usage and a later turn failed
preMortem.consequence: Real consumed usage disappears from the ledger aggregate (dishonest under-count)
preMortem.mitigation: recordFinalForHost consults the failure lane ONLY when scanCodexTurnCompletedUsage returned null; smoke pins a usage+failure precedence case asserting provider-reported wins

preMortem.scenario: error.message content injects unreadable or oversized text into the ledger row
preMortem.trigger: A failure message carrying newlines, control chars, or multi-KB nested JSON
preMortem.consequence: Ledger rows and CLI summaries become unreadable or bloated
preMortem.mitigation: Digest sanitization: innermost-message extraction, control-char/whitespace collapse, hard 160-char truncation — pinned by a smoke assertion on the digest shape

preMortem.scenario: The second scanner lane breaks the existing usage-lane truncation semantics
preMortem.trigger: Over-cap lines interleaved with usage and failure lines
preMortem.consequence: F-013/F-026 regressions: stale provider-reported finals or spurious usage_line_retention_truncated
preMortem.mitigation: Failure lane uses its own scanner instance with its own flag ignored (fallback-only); existing F-013/F-026 smoke checks must keep passing unchanged
